newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EP endorses new rules on road passenger transport.
newsitem.headline: EP endorses new rules on road passenger transport.

text.p: Draft rules governing national and international road passenger transport got the green light from the European Parliament on Thursday.

Euro-MPs approved a draft regulation -- COM(96)190 -- which sets out the conditions non-resident carriers must fulfil before they can operate national transport services in other EurOpean Union member states.
They also endorsed draft regulation COM(95)729, which updates a 1992 EU rule on international coach and bus services.

Parliament introduced amendments to the proposal on non-resident carriers which aim to protect users against fraud and ensure liberalisation of the sector is accompanied by EU-wide harmonisation of road transport standards.

Rapporteur Mark Killilea warned that unless social, fiscal and technical conditions were harmonised, there would be social dumping and domestic carriers would be tempted to avoid the obligations imposed upon them by sub-contracting to non-residents.

Under EU rules approved in 1992, coach and bus operators are allowed to operate international services if they are already authorised to offer domestic services and comply with EU road transport safety regulations.
The European Commission, which is seeking to liberalise the sector further, is proposing simplifications to the rules.
Euro-MPs, who welcomed the move, called for a number of amendments designed to clarify the text.
